- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2), model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- In high volatility periods (sentiment swings > 0.4), model overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 30d forecast is below 65–68% of recent 18d high, adjust upward by 1–3% to align with historical mean reversion.
- When sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.4 and price < 10% below recent high.
